title: Read one byte sequence two ways
description: You can compare floating-point encoding with integer interpretation of the same bytes.

steps.description: pack with <f encodes 9.81 as a little-endian float. The displayed bytes are c3 f5 1c 41.

steps.question: Does unpack with <i numerically convert the float or interpret its bytes as an integer?
steps.answer: It interprets the same bytes as an integer.

steps.description: The integer interpretation displays 1092416963. This Python snippet illustrates the two C declarations with text and byte operations.
The illustrative symbol tuples contain a name, size, binding, and kind. Both records show gravity with size 4; neither tuple stores float or int.
The contrast packs a double into eight bytes and reads its first four as an integer. The displayed sizes differ, unlike the earlier four-byte pairing.
